title: Retirement Planning Fundamentals and the 4% Rule
content:
Retirement planning is the multi-decade discipline of accumulating sufficient assets to generate predictable income after transitioning out of the active workforce. The goal of retirement planning is achieving financial independence—where portfolio distributions, pensions, and Social Security comfortably cover all living expenses.

A central concept in retirement modeling is the 4% Rule, established by the landmark 1998 Trinity Study. Researchers analyzed historical stock and bond returns across rolling 30-year retirement horizons. They concluded that a retiree with a balanced 50/50 or 60/40 stock-and-bond portfolio could withdraw 4% of their initial portfolio value in year one of retirement, adjust that dollar amount annually for inflation, and have a 95%+ probability of not exhausting their assets over a 30-year period.

The 4% Rule provides a quick way to calculate your target retirement nest egg: simply multiply your anticipated annual retirement expenses by 25. For example, if you estimate needing $60,000 per year from your investments, your target nest egg is $1,500,000 ($60,000 × 25).

Successful retirement accumulation requires leveraging tax-advantaged accounts early in your career. Maximize employer matches in your 401(k), contribute to Roth IRAs, and take advantage of Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) for medical expenses in retirement. As retirement nears, transition asset allocations gradually toward fixed income to mitigate sequence of returns risk.
